desc:
You are given an array candidates of distinct positive integers and two integers k and target. Return every collection of exactly k numbers taken from candidates whose sum is exactly target. A candidate may be used any number of times, including more than once in the same collection.

Two collections are the same if every candidate is used the same number of times, so list each one once with its numbers in non-decreasing order (for example [2,2,3], never [3,2,2]). Rows may be returned in any order. If nothing works, return an empty array.
constraints: The answer has fewer than 3,000 combinations
hints: Plain combination sum has no size limit. Here you also have to track how many numbers are still to be picked.
Sort the candidates and only pick candidates at the current index or later (reuse allowed), so each multiset appears once in sorted order.

With m numbers still to pick and left still to reach, the candidate c is only useful if c * m ≤ left and the largest candidate times m is at least left. Stop the loop or the branch as soon as either test fails.
editorial: Sort the candidates and recurse on (start, m, left): m numbers still to choose and left still to add up. If m == 0, record the current list when left == 0. Otherwise loop i from start; choosing cands[i] recurses with the same i (repetition allowed), m - 1 and left - cands[i].

Two bounds prune the tree. The remaining m numbers are each at least cands[i] (everything before start is excluded), so if cands[i] * m > left this and all later candidates are too big: break. And they are each at most the largest candidate, so if cands[-1] * m < left the branch can never reach the target: return. The number of rows is limited to under 3,000, so the output size stays small.
